title: trustpad moonshot: compliance scratchbook - rowan
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick scratchpad for a lightweight SOC2-ish readiness pass focused on areas that often trip us up when onboarding Dedicated/Private customers (KMS, VPC peering, audit logs, fallback policies). This is messy — working notes + questions to bring to the next trust-ops sync.

High-level goals:
- Surface minimal evidence we can collect in 2 weeks for a baseline audit (security + availability).
- Identify two quick wins that reduce manual evidence collection: log retention policy template, automated snapshot of IAM role assignments.
- Draft a short Q&A for sales engineers mapping typical customer asks to internal controls (e.g., "How do you rotate model encryption keys?").

Assumptions:
- Hosted API has centralized logs in ELK/Vector; Dedicated/Private deploys push agent logs to customer or to our central telemetry depending on contract.
- We have Okta SSO, SCIM provisioning for most employees; some service accounts still use long-lived keys.

Top-of-mind risks / gap hypotheses (ranked quick):
1) Key management sprawl: several legacy workflows still use plaintext API keys mapped to service accounts (risk: confidentiality + unauthorized access).
2) Evidence fragmentation: Dedicated customers' audit logs are stored in different places; we lack a single pointer for auditors (risk: availability of evidence).
3) Inconsistent encryption-at-rest proofs for on-prem packages: packaging/installer docs don't include a signed config demonstrating encryption enabled (risk: confidentiality).
4) Emergency access / break-glass lacks consistent attestation (who signed off, when used).
5) Model variants fallback policy not documented as part of change-management for deployments (processing integrity + availability).

Control mapping (scratch — map to Trust Services categories):
- Security:
  - IAM: Okta SSO + role assignment matrix (evidence: SCIM logs + admin console export).
  - Secrets: KMS usage for model keys + proof of rotation (evidence: KMS rotation logs or rotation policy doc).
  - Network: VPC ingress/egress rules + bastion logs (evidence: infra-as-code + firewall rule history).
- Availability:
  - Capacity provisioning: Dedicated capacity commit records + autoscale policy tests (evidence: capacity plan spreadsheet + test run logs).
  - Monitoring/alerting: per-route latency SLOs + alert test artifacts (evidence: Grafana playbacks, runbooks).
- Confidentiality:
  - Data classification + retention: examples of classification for customer prompt data and retention policy (evidence: policy doc + storage lifecycle).
- Processing Integrity:
  - Model rollout controls: canary policies + rollback history (evidence: console rollout entries, PRs).
- Privacy (if requested): redaction heuristics + PII detection tests (evidence: eval runs).

Concrete evidence items to assemble (minimal set):
- Export: Okta admin user export (CSV snapshot for last 90 days).
- KMS: list of keys used for production; rotation schedule doc (signed).
- Logging: sample ELK query + timestamps showing token-level access for a model inference (anonymized).
- Infra-as-code: commit and plan showing VPC rules for on-prem deploy (include PR link).
- Rollout: a canary deploy entry + rollback event example (PR + console audit entry).
- Emergency access log: last 12 months of break-glass usage (annotated).

Quick operational check commands (notes for SRE/infra):
- IAM snapshot (Okta CLI): okta export-users --filter "lastLogin>2026-01-01" --output csv
- KMS list (gcloud/aws): aws kms list-keys --region us-west-2 | jq '.Keys[]'
- ELK sample query (pseudo): POST /_search { "query": { "term": { "user_id": "redacted" } }, "size": 5 }
- Terraform plan diff for VPC rules: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.type=="aws_security_group")'

Open questions to unblock mapping / evidence collection (to assign):
- Who owns the canonical list of production KMS keys? (assign: infra-kms?)
- Are Dedicated deployment logs piped to our central observability by default or per-customer opt-in? (assign: platform-ops)
- Can we produce an automated export of console rollouts for a date range? (assign: console-team)
- Do we have a retention policy document that explicitly covers "model artifact encryption" for on-prem installers? (assign: packaging)
- Which service accounts still use long-lived API keys and where are those keys stored? (assign: devops inventory)

Draft short Q&A for sales engineers (for customer pre-audit call):
Q: "How do you ensure model inference tokens are not logged in plaintext?"
A: "Our serving runtime scrubs PII from request logs via a configurable redact pipeline; token-level traces are only captured when debugging is enabled and those traces are stored in an encrypted bucket with 90-day retention, accessible via approved audit channels."

Q: "Can customers bring their own KMS/HSM?"
A: "Yes — Private deployments support customer-managed keys (KMS or HSM). We maintain an integration checklist showing required IAM roles and a verification runbook to demonstrate encryption keys in use."

Evidence collection play (two-week plan):
Week 1:
- Day 1-2: Run Okta export + inventory service accounts (deliverable: okta-users-90d.csv, service-account-inventory.md).
- Day 3-4: Ask infra-kms for key list + rotation docs (deliverable: kms-keys.csv, kms-rotation-policy.md).
- Day 5: Collect one example ELK trace anonymized + prepare redaction note (deliverable: elk-sample.json).
Week 2:
- Day 6-7: Snapshot console rollout history for last 6 months (deliverable: rollout-audit.csv).
- Day 8-9: Gather Terraform plan for an on-prem package showing encryption toggles (deliverable: tf-vpc-encrypt-diff.txt).
- Day 10: Produce short one-pager mapping items to TSC categories for auditor.

Two quick wins (low friction):
- Create a small script that exports Okta admin CSV & pushes to a secured share automatically weekly. (owner: infra-tools)
- Add a console endpoint that returns rollout events for a tenant and date range (owner: console-team).

Handy links / refs (placeholders):
- Confluence: privsec/control-mapping-draft
- JIRA: SEC-912 (KMS inventory request)
- GH: infra/terraform#211 (VPC update PR)

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Consider adding a short signed attestation for Private installs: "Installer vX.Y notes encryption enabled" — store signed hash in our artifacts bucket. Could be a one-line file the packager drops during build.
- For Dedicated, is there value in a per-tenant "evidence package" export that bundles: Okta users, KMS key list, rollout CSV, relevant Terraform plan? Would save a lot for audits.
- If we automate evidence packages, think about retention and legal constraints — must avoid bundling PII.

Next steps (for next sync):
- Review assignments, get ACK from infra-kms and platform-ops.
- Draft one-pager auditor-facing.
- Build prototype Okta export script.

-- rowan
(leave this as a living scratchpad; will prune into a formal readiness doc once we have the artifacts)
